The '''2013–14 Ligue 1''' was the 76th season since its establishment.<ref>{{cite news|title=Palmarès: Les champions de France depuis 1932/1933 |url=http://new.lfp.fr/ligue1/palmares |work=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] |access-date=23 April 2011 |language=fr |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110419073300/http://new.lfp.fr/ligue1/palmares |archive-date=19 April 2011 }}</ref> The season began on 9 August 2013 and ended on 17 May 2014. [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] were the [[2012–13 Ligue 1|defending champions]].<ref name="80_ans">{{cite news |title=Présentation de la saison de Ligue 1 |url=http://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/article/presentation-de-la-saison-de-ligue-1.htm |work=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] |date=30 May 2012 |access-date=30 May 2012 |language=fr |archive-date=31 May 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120531224456/http://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/article/presentation-de-la-saison-de-ligue-1.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> As in the previous years, [[Adidas]] provided the official ball for all matches, with a new Adidas Pro Ligue 1 model to be used throughout the season for all matches.<ref>{{cite web|title=Adidas Luncurkan Bola Resmi Ligue 1 2013-2014|url=http://www.bola.net/open-play/adidas-luncurkan-bola-resmi-ligue-1-2013-2014-6cf09d.html|publisher=Bola.net|date=28 May 2013 |access-date=28 May 2013|language=id}}</ref>

On 7 May, Paris Saint-Germain won their second straight Ligue 1 title just before losing 2–1 to [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Rennes]].<ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/27301041|title=PSG celebrate title |date=7 May 2014|work=BBC Sport|access-date=8 May 2014}}</ref>		
The title was secured before PSG kicked off when [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]] drew 1–1 against [[En Avant Guingamp|Guingamp]].<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.espnfc.com/news/story/_/id/1813015/psg-win-second-straight-ligue-1-title?cc=5739|title=PSG gain Ligue 1 title despite loss|date=7 May 2014|work=ESPN|access-date=8 May 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/may/07/paris-saint-germain-clinch-title|title= Paris Saint-Germain clinch title before playing as Guingamp deny Monaco|date=7 May 2014|work=The Guardian|access-date=8 May 2014}}</ref>

== Teams ==
There are three promoted teams from [[Ligue 2]], replacing the three teams that were relegated from Ligue 1 following the [[2012–13 Ligue 1|2012–13 season]]. A total of 20 teams currently compete in the league with three clubs suffering relegation to the second division, Ligue 2. All clubs that secured Ligue 1 status for the season were subject to approval by the [[Direction Nationale du Contrôle de Gestion|DNCG]] before becoming eligible to participate.<ref name = dncg_rulings>The DNCG is responsible for overseeing the legal and financial accounts of professional football clubs in France. If clubs operating in [[French football]] don't meet the DNCG's expectations they can face sanctions such as relegation.</ref>

[[Stade Brestois 29|Brest]] was the first team relegated after a 2–0 home defeat to [[FC Sochaux-Montbéliard|Sochaux]] on 11 May 2013 after 3 years in the top flight. [[AS Nancy|Nancy]] followed one week later after a 2–1 home defeat to [[SC Bastia|Bastia]] on 18 May 2013 ending 8 years of top-flight tenure. Finally [[Troyes AC|Troyes]] were relegated from the top level after a 2–1 away defeat to [[Valenciennes FC|Valenciennes]] on 26 May 2013.

These relegated team were replaced by Ligue 2 champions [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]], runners-up [[En Avant de Guingamp|Guingamp]], and third-placed [[FC Nantes|Nantes]]. Monaco clinched the second division title on 11 May 2013 with two matches to spare after defeating Nîmes 1–0 at away. Monaco made its return to the first division after a two-year absence.

Guingamp and Nantes became the second and third clubs, respectively, to earn promotion to Ligue 1 alongside the champion Monaco. Both clubs achieved promotion with one game to spare following league victories on 17 May 2013. Guingamp returned to the first division after nine years. During its nine-year spell outside the first division, Guingamp also played in [[Championnat National]] in the 2010–11 season. Finally, Nantes, eight-time league champions, returned to top level after a four-year absence.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://int.soccerway.com/national/france/ligue-1/20132014/regular-season/r21342/|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20130613074306/http://int.soccerway.com/national/france/ligue-1/20132014/regular-season/r21342/|url-status= dead|archive-date= 13 June 2013|title=LIGUE 1 FIXTURES 2013-14|work=Soccerway.com|access-date=2 July 2013 }}</ref>
